senses.gloss: f.(b. h.; פָּלַל) [intercession, pleading,] prayer, esp. T’fillah, the Prayer of Benedictions to be said three times every day, four times on the Sabbath and the festivals (v. מוּסַף), and five times on the Day of Atonement and public fast-days (v. נְעִילָה).
units: <cite ref="Taanit 2a:11">Taan. 2ᵃ</cite> <he>ומנלן דבת׳</he> and whence do you prove that the mention of, and the prayer for rain must be inserted in the T’fillah? <cite ref="Taanit 2a:11">Ib.</cite> <he>עבודה שבלב זו ת׳</he>, v. <cite ref="P00026"><he>עֲבוֹדָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 4:1">Ber. IV, 1</cite> <he>תְּפִלַּת השחר</he> the morning T’fillah, <he>ת׳ המנחה</he> the afternoon T’fillah &c. (v. respective determinants).
<cite ref="Berakhot 5a:14">Ib. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>אלו הם יסורין … בטול ת׳</he> sufferings of love are those with which no cessation of prayer is connected.
<cite ref="Berakhot 6b:6">Ib. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>הקובע מקום לתְפִלָּתוֹ</he> he that has a regular place for his prayers.
<cite ref="Berakhot 31b:19">Ib. 31ᵇ</cite> <he>שאסור לישב … של ת׳</he> that it is forbidden to sit down within four cubits distance from one in prayer; a. v. fr.—

<cite ref="Berakhot 31a:26">Ib. 31ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>שומע ת׳</he> (abbrev. <he>ש״ת</he>) ‘hearer of prayer’, the fifteenth section of the Prayer of Benedictions which closes with, ‘blessed be thou, O Lord, the hearer of prayer.’—Pl. <cite ref="V00834"><he>תְּפִלּוֹת</he></cite>, <cite ref="V00832"><he>תְּפִי׳</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Berakhot 26b:4">Ib. 26ᵇ</cite> <he>ת׳ אבות תקנום</he> the patriarchs introduced regular prayers.
<cite ref="Berakhot 26b:4">Ib.</cite> <he>ת׳ כנגד תמידין תקנום</he> prayers (T’filloth) have been instituted so as to correspond to the daily offerings.
<cite ref="Shabbat 30a:5">Sabb. 30ᵃ</cite> <he>כמה ת׳ ותחנונים</he> ever so many prayers and supplications; a. v. fr.
